gloss_relation.reason: The event supports the contamination problem and a clean rerun, but the gloss additionally attributes the process to judgment.
The remark reports wider laboratory participation; calling that participation shared judgment adds an interpretive step without contradicting it.
Formation of the association and its complaint about DNA's favored position directly support the gloss about resentment appearing in professional organizations.
The director's statement that criminalists should work across units directly supports the gloss about an expectation of interchangeability.
The event supports confidence in documentation, but the later reading adds that this confidence helps explain why distant challenges lacked local urgency.
The review episode shows collaborative visual judgment, image selection, and agreement, matching the gloss about joint judgment and persuasive documentation.
The speaker's attack on critics and account of harder testimony support the gloss that the presentation was a defensive response to legitimacy pressure.
The examiner explicitly used defense questioning as a reason to reconsider practice, supporting both the immediate and later glosses about motivation for change.
Tom and Pete directly describe the absence of numerical population-style support and the difficulty of translating firearms judgment into a DNA-like form.
The unit's self-description and repeated identity checks directly support the gloss about intense organization and error avoidance.
The exchange treats disorder and missing labels as violations of expected conduct, supporting the gloss that meticulous organization was an occupational virtue.
Jason's warning connects a tiny procedural check to a ruined sample and consequences for the analyst, directly supporting the gloss about vigilance.
The observation shows pride in the new quantified report, while the gloss additionally links that pride to broader established technique and occupational values.
Taylor's career story shows his own dislike of routine toxicology work, while the gloss generalizes that preference to the narcotics group.
Tim both rejects imprecise wording and refuses an unsupported claim about purity, directly supporting the gloss about precision and bounded conclusions.
The exchange shows Tim and Taylor valuing redundant documentation, but the gloss extends that value to the laboratory as a whole.
The meeting clearly shows concern with processing speed, while the gloss additionally positions efficiency alongside the unit's broader commitment to thorough analysis.
Jodi directly links the possible loss of crystal testing to reviewability, speed, and a likely shift toward slower instrument work, matching the gloss.
Taylor contrasts specialized crystal training with easy instrument operation; the gloss adds the broader meaning of that contrast for craft expertise and judgment.
Billie explicitly ties her preference for crystal work to practicing chemistry and avoiding repetitive instrument work, matching the gloss about variety and craft involvement.
